improv_extras.concept: arrange particles on a Poincare-disk hyperbolic tiling so cells shrink toward the rim — non-Euclidean, infinite-edge composition

v1.feedback: The leaf-vein fragment shader is genuinely lovely and the bone/sage/ash palette is exactly right, but this reads as a fresh Poincaré-disk piece rather than a morph of parent sdj — chain mode demands visible lineage from the parent form, not a clean-slate herbarium. The concentric-ring approximation of hyperbolic tiling (tanh-spaced rings with increasing cell count) is readable but could push harder toward true Möbius-transformed polygonal cells so the Escher reference lands in 2 seconds. Consider inheriting sdj's geometry or motion signature and letting the hyperbolic tiling emerge as a tessellation mapped onto that existing form.
